pages.text: The river rose, then fell a little. All sorts of things had washed onto the bank. Mom and the three children each chose something.
Sonu wanted the best thing. Quickly picking up a piece of wood, Sonu said, "Mine!"
Sonu picked up two more: two in one hand, one in the other.
Raju said, "Choose only one." Sonu hid both hands behind their back.
A large piece of wood rested at the water's edge, smooth and shiny.
Mina lifted it with both hands.
Sonu's hands were full. Sonu could only stamp their feet.
Mom spread both hands wide, then picked up one pebble in one hand.
Sonu put all three pieces of wood on the sand. Both hands were empty.
A tree stump lay at the water's edge, roots stretching like horns. Sonu hugged it up with both hands.
